newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Safras sees 26.28 mln tonne soybean crop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Safras sees 26.28 mln tonne soybean crop.

text.p: Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop should reach 26.28 million tonnes, down 0.4 percent from the previous forecast but up from a revised 23.49 million tonnes in 1995/96, said independent consultants Safras e Mercado.
Planted area is expected to total 11.36 million hectares, down 1.4 percent on the previous forecast of 11.51 million hectares but still up around 4.3 percent on the area planted last year.

"The rise in the planted area of soybeans is attributed, among other factors, to the lower growth level of the global and South American harvest in relation with the rise in consumption, which is supporting external and internal prices," Safras said.
Other factors included the abolition of the ICMS export tax, regular rains in most producing regions and the positive outlook for prices in 1997, it said.
But lack of financing prevented a more significant rise in the cultivation of soybeans, Safras added.
Parana should remain the biggest producer with forecast output of 6.7 million tonnes, up from 6.45 million last year.

But Safras revised downwards its earlier forecast for Rio Grande do Sul to 5.7 million tonnes from 6.0 million tonnes, saying planted area was less than originally expected because of the severe credit problems farmers faced. The region usually is the largest producing state but yielded just 4.4 million tonnes last year due to prolonged drought.
Mato Grosso benefited from good weather conditions so that output should reach 5.02 million tonnes, up slightly on the first estimate, Safras said.
Safras forecast a jump in overseas soybean sales due to the abolition of the ICMS export tax. Excess production is seen being exported, leaving crushing levels roughly stable.

"Stocks of soymeal and soyoil should remain low, given that the possible drop in exports of the sub-products would be compensated by greater domestic consumption," Safras e Mercado said in its weekly newsletter.
"For this reason, it is possible to imagine a favourable price scenario for the Brazilian soybean producer in 1997, although well below 1996, still at least 10 to 15 percent above average," it added.
In its second estimate for the 1996/97 crop, Safras revised slightly upwards its figure for 1995/96 from its last forecast of 23.29 million tonnes.
This was because of higher production than earlier anticipated in states including Goias, Mato Grosso do Sul and smaller producing states like Santa Catarina and Maranhao.
